translations.text: And in the bush there was a fire that only gave light, without any power to burn, as the Psalm testifies when it says:
"The voice of the Lord divides the flame of fire." So this mystical saying teaches us that then, at the repayment for deeds, its light will be set apart to be the delight of the saints,
and its painful burning will be set apart as torment for the punishment of sinners. And again, from what happens to the moon we can find the truth: its whole body is not used up,
but the light that is in it withdraws, and it seems to us that it is being added to [?] they appear in it [?]. They testify that its body is not destroyed.
For you can easily see this when the air is clear, when its disc is without light: just as you see it from its one part, you may see the other part that is unlit.

And do not think that the light of the moon is made complete by something else [?], because its light decreases when it comes near the sun, and when it moves away [?] three days [?] to investigate this [?],
but I tell you that its body is something different, and the illuminating light is mixed into it in such a way that it is not separated from it.
But as for the moon, insofar as it points to the truth [?], these too were commanded to divide between day and night.
And above it was said that God divided between light and darkness, for at that time he made their natures separate, so that they would have no fellowship with one another,
light with darkness and darkness with light. Shadow is darkness [?]. It occurs when the light is blocked by some body,
and in the morning it stretches out toward the evening, and [in the evening?] it leans toward the east [?]; seen [?] from the earth, this is the nature of night.
And this is what was meant by the saying that God divided between the light and between the darkness,
for darkness flees from light, and their opposition to one another [?]. The sun was commanded to rule [?] when the disc is filled, and the two [?] the sun [?],
and the moon goes down into a dark place, and when the sun is full [?], it sometimes rises [?]. If the moon's light is not complete in its shape at night,
this does not contradict what was said. Rather, when it is full, it has power over the night,
and it outshines the stars in brightness and lights up the whole earth evenly. "And let them be for signs": the signs given by the luminaries are useful for human life,
as long as no one goes beyond due measure in investigating them, and learns their [?] and the [?] of the winds, which can be seen from the sun and from the visible signs of the sun.
In this way you can see what is going to happen. When the sky is overcast and its brightness is red, and its colour looks red and the colour of glowing embers,
the thickness of the air creates this kind of sight for the eyes. And when the air, standing still, is not dispersed by the brightness of the sun,
it signals that there is a great deal of vapour from the earth in the air, and that it has brought rain to the places where it gathers.
And likewise the moon and the sun, when there are what are called 'rings' [?] surrounding them,
signal very heavy rains. And again, what is called an anthelion, when it gathers on the sun's path, is a sign of disturbances in the air.
